Football tournament

The **Campeonato de España–Copa de Su Majestad el Rey**,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-1) commonly known as **Copa del Rey**,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-2)La Copa[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-3) or (in [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_language "English language")) the **Spanish Cup**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-4) or King's Cup, and formerly known as Copa del Presidente de la República[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-5) (1932–1936) and Copa del Generalísimo[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-6) (1939–1976), is an annual [knockout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament "Single-elimination tournament")[football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") competition in [Spanish football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_in_Spain "Football in Spain"), organized by the [Royal Spanish Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Spanish_Football_Federation "Royal Spanish Football Federation").

The competition was founded in 1903, making it the oldest Spanish football competition played at a national level. Copa del Rey winners qualify for the following season's [UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League"). If they have already qualified for Europe through their league position, the Europa League spot is given to the highest-placed team in the league who has not yet qualified (until 2014 this place was awarded to the Copa runners-up, unless they too had already qualified via the league).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-gibraltar-7)

[Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") is the most successful club in the competition, having won 32 titles. [Athletic Bilbao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletic_Bilbao "Athletic Bilbao") has the second-most wins with 24, while [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") is third with 20. [Real Sociedad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Sociedad "Real Sociedad") is the current title holder, having defeated [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") in the [2026 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Copa_del_Rey_final "2026 Copa del Rey final") held at the [Estadio de La Cartuja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_de_La_Cartuja "Estadio de La Cartuja").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Copa_del_Rey&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

In 1902, a competition under the name **[Copa de la Coronación](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1902_Copa_de_la_Coronaci%C3%B3n "1902 Copa de la Coronación")** was played after Juan de Astorquia, President of [Bilbao Football Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bilbao_Football_Club "Bilbao Football Club"), and [Carlos Padrós](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Padr%C3%B3s "Carlos Padrós"), later president of [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF"), suggested a football tournament to celebrate the coronation of Spanish [King Alfonso XIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfonso_XIII "Alfonso XIII"). Four other teams joined [Madrid FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") for the competition: [FC Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona"), [Club Español de Foot-Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCD_Espanyol "RCD Espanyol"), [New Foot-Ball de Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Foot-Ball_Club "New Foot-Ball Club") and [Club Bizcaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bizcaya_(football_team) "Bizcaya (football team)") (a team made up of players from Athletic Club and Bilbao FC), which eventually defeated Barcelona in the final. That cup is on display in the [Athletic Bilbao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletic_Bilbao "Athletic Bilbao") museum and the club includes the victory as the first of its Copa del Rey wins, but the [Royal Spanish Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Spanish_Football_Federation "Royal Spanish Football Federation") officially does not recognise it as such, only considering it to be the forerunner of the Copa del Rey.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-:0-8)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-9)

The Copa del Rey was effectively Spain's national football championship from 1903 (the first edition won by Athletic Bilbao with Juan de Astorquia as captain and president)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-Marca-Palmar%C3%A9s-10) until the foundation of the _Campeonato de Liga_—League Championship ([La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga"))—in 1929. It was initially known as the _Copa del Ayuntamiento de Madrid_ (Madrid City Council's Cup). Between 1905 and 1932, it was known as the _Copa de Su Majestad El Rey Alfonso XIII_ (His Majesty King Alfonso XIII's Cup). During the [Second Spanish Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Spanish_Republic "Second Spanish Republic"), it was known as the _Copa del Presidente de la República_ (President of the Republic Cup) or _Copa de España_ (Spanish Cup) and during the years of [Francisco Franco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Franco "Francisco Franco")'s [Spanish State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_State "Spanish State"), it was known as the _Copa de Su Excelencia El Generalísimo_ or _Copa del Generalísimo_ (His Excellency, The Supreme General's Cup).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-Marca-Palmar%C3%A9s-10)

Athletic Bilbao were declared winners in 1904 after their opponents [Español de Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Espa%C3%B1ol_de_Madrid "Club Español de Madrid") failed to show up. Between 1903 and 1909 the competition was organized by [Madrid FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid "Real Madrid") or by the Madrid Federation. Afterwards, it was taken over by the FECF (_Federación Española de Clubs de Football_), a forerunner of the RFEF.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-11) However, in both 1910 and 1913 there was a split among the clubs and two parallel competitions were held, one organized by the FECF and the other by the UECF (_Unión Española de Club de Football_). All these editions are officially recognized by the RFEF.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-winners-rfef-12)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-13) In 1937, during the [Spanish Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Civil_War "Spanish Civil War"), clubs in the [Republican area of Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_faction_(Spanish_Civil_War) "Republican faction (Spanish Civil War)") entered the [Copa de la España Libre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_de_la_Espa%C3%B1a_Libre "Copa de la España Libre"), with [Levante FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levante_FC "Levante FC") (forerunner of the present [Levante UD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levante_UD "Levante UD")) beating their city rivals [Valencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencia_CF "Valencia CF") 1–0 in the final. Although in 2009 the [Congress of Deputies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_Deputies_(Spain) "Congress of Deputies (Spain)") urged the [Royal Spanish Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Spanish_Football_Federation "Royal Spanish Football Federation") to recognise it as a Copa del Rey win for Levante,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-14) for several years the governing body of Spanish football made no decision on the matter.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-15) On 25 March 2023, the tournament was officially recognized by the RFEF,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-Copa_Espa%C3%B1a_oficial-16)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-reconoce_2023-17) but not as a Copa del Rey.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-winners-rfef-12)

Because of the dispute regarding the 1902 competition, the statistics regarding the leading winners are also disputed. Barcelona have won the Copa 32 times; Athletic Bilbao are in second place, with either 24 or 25 titles, depending on the source.

Before the formation of La Liga in 1929, the competition was in essence a national championship. Teams qualified to enter via their regional leagues. Over the years, various formats, including group stages have been used. [Reserve teams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reserve_team "Reserve team") of the professional clubs, who compete in lower divisions of the league pyramid, were permitted to take part until 1990. For a number of years, only teams from the [_Primera División_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga"), [_Segunda A_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Segunda_Divisi%C3%B3n "Segunda División"), about 23 teams from the [_Segunda B_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Second_Division_B "Spanish Second Division B") and the 17 _[Tercera División](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tercera\_Divisi%C3%B3n "Tercera División")_ champions (or runners-up if the champion was a reserve team) were invited to enter, giving a total of 83. Amended rules for the 2019–20 edition led to the number of entrants increasing to 125 (later to 126 in 2025), including winners of the [regional divisions at the fifth level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divisiones_Regionales_de_F%C3%BAtbol "Divisiones Regionales de Fútbol").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-18)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-19)

Since the format overhaul, all rounds are single-leg ties with lower division teams hosting the match and the majority of the top-level clubs entering at the first Round (four teams taking part in the [Supercopa de España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a "Supercopa de España") entering in the third round – last 32), other than the semi-final stage which is played over two legs. This is another change introduced in 2019–20, with prior editions involving two legs from the point at which the top-tier clubs entered in the fourth round (last 32). Athletic Bilbao particularly embraced the new format, winning a total of 22 single-leg ties to reach the two-legged semi-finals in each of its first five seasons[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-20) before losing to [Osasuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CA_Osasuna "CA Osasuna") in the [2024–25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_Copa_del_Rey "2024–25 Copa del Rey") Round of 16. The final is a one-off game played at a neutral venue, with [Seville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seville "Seville") becoming the regular home.

The winners qualify for both the following season's Supercopa de España and [UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League"); in the past, the runners-up often played in the Supercopa if the winners had also finished as league champions (although on some earlier occasions in these circumstances, no Supercopa match was played and the [double winners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_(association_football) "Double (association football)") were awarded the title by default). From the [2019–20 Supercopa de España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a "2019–20 Supercopa de España") edition onwards, the previous Copa del Rey runners-up automatically qualify in addition to the winners with four teams taking part in the event.

Throughout the history of the competition, there have been 12 actual trophies, which were permanently awarded to clubs for winning the competition either three times in a row or on five occasions, and for other special reasons. Thus, five trophies have been permanently awarded to Barcelona, three to Athletic Bilbao and one to Real Madrid (the last _Copa de la República_ in 1936). Athletic kept the first trophy as inaugural winners, [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC") were awarded the _Trofeo del Generalísimo_ after its first edition in 1939 and [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid"), winners the previous year, were awarded the 11th trophy following the death of Francisco Franco in 1976.

On 22 December 2010, at an [extraordinary general meeting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extraordinary_general_meeting "Extraordinary general meeting") of the Royal Spanish Football Federation, Sevilla requested permission from the Federation to keep the trophy they had won in the [2010 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Copa_del_Rey_Final "2010 Copa del Rey Final") to commemorate the victory of the [Spain national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_men's_national_football_team "Spain men's national football team") at the [2010 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup "2010 FIFA World Cup") in [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-21) A new trophy was made by [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") jeweler Federico Alegre. The trophy, made of silver, weighs 15 kg (33 lb) and is 75 cm (30 in) tall. On 21 April 2011, Real Madrid became the first recipients. During the post-game celebrations, the trophy was accidentally dropped by Real Madrid player [Sergio Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Ramos "Sergio Ramos") from the top of a [double-decker bus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-decker_bus "Double-decker bus"), which then ran over it. Ten pieces were found by civil servicemen when they recovered it from the ground at [Plaza de Cibeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaza_de_Cibeles "Plaza de Cibeles"). The club received a copy which is displayed at [Santiago Bernabéu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_Stadium "Santiago Bernabéu Stadium").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-22)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-23)

The new presidency of [Luis Rubiales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Rubiales "Luis Rubiales") initiated profound restructuring within the Federation.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-24)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-25)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-26) These changes impacted competitions organized by the organization, specifically the Copa del Rey and the [Supercopa de España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a "Supercopa de España"). Both were reformed with new formats designed to increase competitiveness and attractiveness.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-27) In the case of the Supercopa, the changes had a reciprocal effect; the Copa champion and runner-up were included alongside the league championship's top two finishers, creating a four-team competition.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-28)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-29)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-2019CAMBIOS-30) Beginning with the 2019–20 edition, the cup championship introduced a significant change: the designation of a fixed venue for the final; the [Estadio de La Cartuja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_de_La_Cartuja "Estadio de La Cartuja") in Seville was chosen to host the final for a four-year period.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-2019CAMBIOS-30)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-31)

## Broadcasters

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Copa_del_Rey&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Broadcasters")]

From the [2019–20 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Copa_del_Rey "2019–20 Copa del Rey"), the final match is already included in La Copa broadcasting rights package.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-50) Previously, the final match is excluded in selected countries (other broadcasters (including Spain) will receive the [Supercopa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a "Supercopa de España") rights after covering a Copa final match) due to laws and regulations of the tournament broadcasting rights by [CNMC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comisi%C3%B3n_Nacional_de_los_Mercados_y_la_Competencia "Comisión Nacional de los Mercados y la Competencia") in Spain. In a separate deal, streamer [Ibai Llanos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibai_Llanos "Ibai Llanos") would broadcast the [2026 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Copa_del_Rey_final "2026 Copa del Rey final") on his personal YouTube channel.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-51)

## Notes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Copa_del_Rey&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Notes")]

A.**^** En route to the final, Español de Madrid had tied one game and had not completed the other game, which led Athletic Bilbao to file a complaint. Faced with this problem and unable to quickly resolve the case, the Madrid Association decided to award the cup to Athletic as defending champions.

B.**^** Playing as _Club Ciclista de San Sebastián_.

C.**^** Playing as _Vasconia de San Sebastián_.

D.**^** A mini-group of three teams was played, with Athletic Bilbao defeating [Madrid FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") 2–0 a day before their win over Vasconia, thus the match between the Basque teams was decisive in deciding the winner, although not a typical final (Vasconia then played Madrid the following day to complete the group, also winning 2–0).

E.**^** The first final, played the day earlier, ended 2–2 after extra time.

F.**^** Originally played as a two-legged final. The first match, played seven days earlier, ended 2–2, and the second match, played six days earlier, ended 0–0.

G.**^** The first final, played two days earlier, ended 0–0 after extra time.

H.**^** The first and second final ended 1–1 after extra time. Both matches were played a month before the second replay.

I.**^** Real Madrid won the penalty shoot-out 4–3.

J.**^** Betis won the penalty shoot-out 8–7.

K.**^** Real Sociedad won the penalty shoot-out 4–2.

L.**^** Zaragoza won the penalty shoot-out 5–4.

M.**^** The match was suspended by heavy rain and hail in the 79th minute, and was resumed three days later.

N.**^** Barcelona won the penalty shoot-out 5–4.

The **Campeonato de España–Copa de Su Majestad el Rey**,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-1) commonly known as **Copa del Rey**,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-2)La Copa[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-3) or (in [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_language "English language")) the **Spanish Cup**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-4) or King's Cup, and formerly known as Copa del Presidente de la República[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-5) (1932–1936) and Copa del Generalísimo[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-6) (1939–1976), is an annual [knockout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament "Single-elimination tournament")[football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") competition in [Spanish football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_in_Spain "Football in Spain"), organized by the [Royal Spanish Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Spanish_Football_Federation "Royal Spanish Football Federation").

The competition was founded in 1903, making it the oldest Spanish football competition played at a national level. Copa del Rey winners qualify for the following season's [UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League"). If they have already qualified for Europe through their league position, the Europa League spot is given to the highest-placed team in the league who has not yet qualified (until 2014 this place was awarded to the Copa runners-up, unless they too had already qualified via the league).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-gibraltar-7)

[Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") is the most successful club in the competition, having won 32 titles. [Athletic Bilbao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletic_Bilbao "Athletic Bilbao") has the second-most wins with 24, while [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") is third with 20. [Real Sociedad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Sociedad "Real Sociedad") is the current title holder, having defeated [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") in the [2026 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Copa_del_Rey_final "2026 Copa del Rey final") held at the [Estadio de La Cartuja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_de_La_Cartuja "Estadio de La Cartuja").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Copa_del_Rey&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

In 1902, a competition under the name **[Copa de la Coronación](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1902_Copa_de_la_Coronaci%C3%B3n "1902 Copa de la Coronación")** was played after Juan de Astorquia, President of [Bilbao Football Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bilbao_Football_Club "Bilbao Football Club"), and [Carlos Padrós](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Padr%C3%B3s "Carlos Padrós"), later president of [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF"), suggested a football tournament to celebrate the coronation of Spanish [King Alfonso XIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfonso_XIII "Alfonso XIII"). Four other teams joined [Madrid FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") for the competition: [FC Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona"), [Club Español de Foot-Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCD_Espanyol "RCD Espanyol"), [New Foot-Ball de Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Foot-Ball_Club "New Foot-Ball Club") and [Club Bizcaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bizcaya_(football_team) "Bizcaya (football team)") (a team made up of players from Athletic Club and Bilbao FC), which eventually defeated Barcelona in the final. That cup is on display in the [Athletic Bilbao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletic_Bilbao "Athletic Bilbao") museum and the club includes the victory as the first of its Copa del Rey wins, but the [Royal Spanish Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Spanish_Football_Federation "Royal Spanish Football Federation") officially does not recognise it as such, only considering it to be the forerunner of the Copa del Rey.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-:0-8)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-9)

The Copa del Rey was effectively Spain's national football championship from 1903 (the first edition won by Athletic Bilbao with Juan de Astorquia as captain and president)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-Marca-Palmar%C3%A9s-10) until the foundation of the _Campeonato de Liga_—League Championship ([La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga"))—in 1929. It was initially known as the _Copa del Ayuntamiento de Madrid_ (Madrid City Council's Cup). Between 1905 and 1932, it was known as the _Copa de Su Majestad El Rey Alfonso XIII_ (His Majesty King Alfonso XIII's Cup). During the [Second Spanish Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Spanish_Republic "Second Spanish Republic"), it was known as the _Copa del Presidente de la República_ (President of the Republic Cup) or _Copa de España_ (Spanish Cup) and during the years of [Francisco Franco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Franco "Francisco Franco")'s [Spanish State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_State "Spanish State"), it was known as the _Copa de Su Excelencia El Generalísimo_ or _Copa del Generalísimo_ (His Excellency, The Supreme General's Cup).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-Marca-Palmar%C3%A9s-10)

Athletic Bilbao were declared winners in 1904 after their opponents [Español de Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Espa%C3%B1ol_de_Madrid "Club Español de Madrid") failed to show up. Between 1903 and 1909 the competition was organized by [Madrid FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid "Real Madrid") or by the Madrid Federation. Afterwards, it was taken over by the FECF (_Federación Española de Clubs de Football_), a forerunner of the RFEF.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-11) However, in both 1910 and 1913 there was a split among the clubs and two parallel competitions were held, one organized by the FECF and the other by the UECF (_Unión Española de Club de Football_). All these editions are officially recognized by the RFEF.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-winners-rfef-12)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-13) In 1937, during the [Spanish Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Civil_War "Spanish Civil War"), clubs in the [Republican area of Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_faction_(Spanish_Civil_War) "Republican faction (Spanish Civil War)") entered the [Copa de la España Libre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_de_la_Espa%C3%B1a_Libre "Copa de la España Libre"), with [Levante FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levante_FC "Levante FC") (forerunner of the present [Levante UD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levante_UD "Levante UD")) beating their city rivals [Valencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencia_CF "Valencia CF") 1–0 in the final. Although in 2009 the [Congress of Deputies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_Deputies_(Spain) "Congress of Deputies (Spain)") urged the [Royal Spanish Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Spanish_Football_Federation "Royal Spanish Football Federation") to recognise it as a Copa del Rey win for Levante,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-14) for several years the governing body of Spanish football made no decision on the matter.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-15) On 25 March 2023, the tournament was officially recognized by the RFEF,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-Copa_Espa%C3%B1a_oficial-16)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-reconoce_2023-17) but not as a Copa del Rey.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-winners-rfef-12)

Because of the dispute regarding the 1902 competition, the statistics regarding the leading winners are also disputed. Barcelona have won the Copa 32 times; Athletic Bilbao are in second place, with either 24 or 25 titles, depending on the source.

Before the formation of La Liga in 1929, the competition was in essence a national championship. Teams qualified to enter via their regional leagues. Over the years, various formats, including group stages have been used. [Reserve teams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reserve_team "Reserve team") of the professional clubs, who compete in lower divisions of the league pyramid, were permitted to take part until 1990. For a number of years, only teams from the [_Primera División_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga"), [_Segunda A_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Segunda_Divisi%C3%B3n "Segunda División"), about 23 teams from the [_Segunda B_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Second_Division_B "Spanish Second Division B") and the 17 _[Tercera División](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tercera\_Divisi%C3%B3n "Tercera División")_ champions (or runners-up if the champion was a reserve team) were invited to enter, giving a total of 83. Amended rules for the 2019–20 edition led to the number of entrants increasing to 125 (later to 126 in 2025), including winners of the [regional divisions at the fifth level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divisiones_Regionales_de_F%C3%BAtbol "Divisiones Regionales de Fútbol").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-18)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-19)

Since the format overhaul, all rounds are single-leg ties with lower division teams hosting the match and the majority of the top-level clubs entering at the first Round (four teams taking part in the [Supercopa de España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a "Supercopa de España") entering in the third round – last 32), other than the semi-final stage which is played over two legs. This is another change introduced in 2019–20, with prior editions involving two legs from the point at which the top-tier clubs entered in the fourth round (last 32). Athletic Bilbao particularly embraced the new format, winning a total of 22 single-leg ties to reach the two-legged semi-finals in each of its first five seasons[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-20) before losing to [Osasuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CA_Osasuna "CA Osasuna") in the [2024–25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_Copa_del_Rey "2024–25 Copa del Rey") Round of 16. The final is a one-off game played at a neutral venue, with [Seville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seville "Seville") becoming the regular home.

The winners qualify for both the following season's Supercopa de España and [UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League"); in the past, the runners-up often played in the Supercopa if the winners had also finished as league champions (although on some earlier occasions in these circumstances, no Supercopa match was played and the [double winners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_(association_football) "Double (association football)") were awarded the title by default). From the [2019–20 Supercopa de España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a "2019–20 Supercopa de España") edition onwards, the previous Copa del Rey runners-up automatically qualify in addition to the winners with four teams taking part in the event.

Throughout the history of the competition, there have been 12 actual trophies, which were permanently awarded to clubs for winning the competition either three times in a row or on five occasions, and for other special reasons. Thus, five trophies have been permanently awarded to Barcelona, three to Athletic Bilbao and one to Real Madrid (the last _Copa de la República_ in 1936). Athletic kept the first trophy as inaugural winners, [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC") were awarded the _Trofeo del Generalísimo_ after its first edition in 1939 and [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid"), winners the previous year, were awarded the 11th trophy following the death of Francisco Franco in 1976.

On 22 December 2010, at an [extraordinary general meeting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extraordinary_general_meeting "Extraordinary general meeting") of the Royal Spanish Football Federation, Sevilla requested permission from the Federation to keep the trophy they had won in the [2010 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Copa_del_Rey_Final "2010 Copa del Rey Final") to commemorate the victory of the [Spain national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_men's_national_football_team "Spain men's national football team") at the [2010 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup "2010 FIFA World Cup") in [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-21) A new trophy was made by [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") jeweler Federico Alegre. The trophy, made of silver, weighs 15 kg (33 lb) and is 75 cm (30 in) tall. On 21 April 2011, Real Madrid became the first recipients. During the post-game celebrations, the trophy was accidentally dropped by Real Madrid player [Sergio Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Ramos "Sergio Ramos") from the top of a [double-decker bus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-decker_bus "Double-decker bus"), which then ran over it. Ten pieces were found by civil servicemen when they recovered it from the ground at [Plaza de Cibeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaza_de_Cibeles "Plaza de Cibeles"). The club received a copy which is displayed at [Santiago Bernabéu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_Stadium "Santiago Bernabéu Stadium").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-22)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-23)

The new presidency of [Luis Rubiales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Rubiales "Luis Rubiales") initiated profound restructuring within the Federation.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-24)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-25)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-26) These changes impacted competitions organized by the organization, specifically the Copa del Rey and the [Supercopa de España](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a "Supercopa de España"). Both were reformed with new formats designed to increase competitiveness and attractiveness.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-27) In the case of the Supercopa, the changes had a reciprocal effect; the Copa champion and runner-up were included alongside the league championship's top two finishers, creating a four-team competition.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-28)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-29)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-2019CAMBIOS-30) Beginning with the 2019–20 edition, the cup championship introduced a significant change: the designation of a fixed venue for the final; the [Estadio de La Cartuja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_de_La_Cartuja "Estadio de La Cartuja") in Seville was chosen to host the final for a four-year period.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-2019CAMBIOS-30)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-31)

## Individual records

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Copa_del_Rey&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Individual records")]

Main article: [Football records and statistics in Spain §Copa del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_records_and_statistics_in_Spain#Copa_del_Rey "Football records and statistics in Spain")

*   Most goals scored: 81 – [Telmo Zarra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telmo_Zarra "Telmo Zarra")
*   Most goals scored in finals: 9 – [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi")[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-46)
*   Most finals scored in: 7 – [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi")[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-47)
*   Most assists provided in finals: 6 – [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi")
*   Most man of the match awards won in finals: 3 – [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi")
*   Most appearances made in finals: 10 – [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi") and Sergio Busquets[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-48)
*   Most cup wins: 7 – [José Maria Belauste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mar%C3%ADa_Belauste "José María Belauste"), [Piru Gaínza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agust%C3%ADn_Ga%C3%ADnza "Agustín Gaínza"), [Gerard Piqué](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerard_Piqu%C3%A9 "Gerard Piqué"), [Sergio Busquets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Busquets "Sergio Busquets") and [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi")[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-49)

## Broadcasters

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Copa_del_Rey&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Broadcasters")]

From the [2019–20 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Copa_del_Rey "2019–20 Copa del Rey"), the final match is already included in La Copa broadcasting rights package.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-50) Previously, the final match is excluded in selected countries (other broadcasters (including Spain) will receive the [Supercopa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercopa_de_Espa%C3%B1a "Supercopa de España") rights after covering a Copa final match) due to laws and regulations of the tournament broadcasting rights by [CNMC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comisi%C3%B3n_Nacional_de_los_Mercados_y_la_Competencia "Comisión Nacional de los Mercados y la Competencia") in Spain. In a separate deal, streamer [Ibai Llanos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibai_Llanos "Ibai Llanos") would broadcast the [2026 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Copa_del_Rey_final "2026 Copa del Rey final") on his personal YouTube channel.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-51)

## Notes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Copa_del_Rey&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Notes")]

A.**^** En route to the final, Español de Madrid had tied one game and had not completed the other game, which led Athletic Bilbao to file a complaint. Faced with this problem and unable to quickly resolve the case, the Madrid Association decided to award the cup to Athletic as defending champions.

B.**^** Playing as _Club Ciclista de San Sebastián_.

C.**^** Playing as _Vasconia de San Sebastián_.

D.**^** A mini-group of three teams was played, with Athletic Bilbao defeating [Madrid FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") 2–0 a day before their win over Vasconia, thus the match between the Basque teams was decisive in deciding the winner, although not a typical final (Vasconia then played Madrid the following day to complete the group, also winning 2–0).

E.**^** The first final, played the day earlier, ended 2–2 after extra time.

F.**^** Originally played as a two-legged final. The first match, played seven days earlier, ended 2–2, and the second match, played six days earlier, ended 0–0.

G.**^** The first final, played two days earlier, ended 0–0 after extra time.

H.**^** The first and second final ended 1–1 after extra time. Both matches were played a month before the second replay.

I.**^** Real Madrid won the penalty shoot-out 4–3.

J.**^** Betis won the penalty shoot-out 8–7.

K.**^** Real Sociedad won the penalty shoot-out 4–2.

L.**^** Zaragoza won the penalty shoot-out 5–4.

M.**^** The match was suspended by heavy rain and hail in the 79th minute, and was resumed three days later.

N.**^** Barcelona won the penalty shoot-out 5–4.

The **1970–71 Copa del Generalísimo** was the 69th staging of the Spanish Cup[football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") competition. It began on 14 October 1970 and concluded on 4 July 1971 with the final.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The **1970–71 Copa del Generalísimo** was the 69th staging of the Spanish Cup[football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") competition. It began on 14 October 1970 and concluded on 4 July 1971 with the final.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The **1974–75 Copa del Generalísimo** was the 73rd staging of the Spanish Cup. The competition began on 30 October 1974 and ended on 5 July 1975.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

The **1978–79 Copa del Rey** was the 77th staging of the Spanish Cup. The competition began on 20 September 1978 and concluded on 30 June 1979 with the final.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_][Valencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencia_CF "Valencia CF") won the cup.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978%E2%80%9379_Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-1)

The **1978–79 Copa del Rey** was the 77th staging of the Spanish Cup. The competition began on 20 September 1978 and concluded on 30 June 1979 with the final.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_][Valencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencia_CF "Valencia CF") won the cup.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1978%E2%80%9379_Copa_del_Rey#cite_note-1)

The **1973–74 Copa del Generalísimo** was the 72nd staging of the Spanish Cup. The competition began on 26 September 1973 and concluded on 28 June 1974 with the final.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The **1973–74 Copa del Generalísimo** was the 72nd staging of the Spanish Cup. The competition began on 26 September 1973 and concluded on 28 June 1974 with the final.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The **1976–77 [DFB-Pokal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DFB-Pokal "DFB-Pokal")** was the 34th season of the annual German [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") cup competition. It began on 6 August 1976 and ended on 30 May 1977. 128 teams competed in the tournament of seven rounds. In the final [1. FC Köln](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1._FC_K%C3%B6ln "1. FC Köln") defeated [Hertha BSC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hertha_BSC "Hertha BSC") 1–0 in a replay after the first game ended in a draw after 120 minutes. It was the only DFB-Pokal final ever to be replayed.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976%E2%80%9377_DFB-Pokal#cite_note-1)

The **1976–77 [DFB-Pokal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DFB-Pokal "DFB-Pokal")** was the 34th season of the annual German [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") cup competition. It began on 6 August 1976 and ended on 30 May 1977. 128 teams competed in the tournament of seven rounds. In the final [1. FC Köln](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1._FC_K%C3%B6ln "1. FC Köln") defeated [Hertha BSC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hertha_BSC "Hertha BSC") 1–0 in a replay after the first game ended in a draw after 120 minutes. It was the only DFB-Pokal final ever to be replayed.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976%E2%80%9377_DFB-Pokal#cite_note-1)

The **1976–77 Copa del Rey** was the 75th staging of the Spanish Cup. The competition began on 22 September 1976 and concluded on 25 June 1977 with the final.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The **1976–77 Copa del Rey** was the 75th staging of the Spanish Cup. The competition began on 22 September 1976 and concluded on 25 June 1977 with the final.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

and scope. Never replace relevant rows with ellipses, examples or instructions to

and explicitly mark omissions. A partial, restricted or truncated list is not the
complete candidate set. Missing fields are unknown. Keep relevant discoveries even
if they answer a different part of the original question.

Follow links likely to fill a candidate's missing condition or reach the required

try a detail page or another supported route. Links outside the menu and inferred
paths on an observed site are allowed. Child notes are returned automatically;
do not copy their facts into your own note. Retain useful unvisited links even
when expansion stops.

**Next links:** Useful URLs and the missing field each could establish.

incomplete evidence, or not_found with a brief reason. During navigation, call

The **1974–75 Copa del Generalísimo** was the 73rd staging of the Spanish Cup. The competition began on 30 October 1974 and ended on 5 July 1975.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The **1974–75 Copa del Generalísimo** was the 73rd staging of the Spanish Cup. The competition began on 30 October 1974 and ended on 5 July 1975.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Main article: 1974–75 Copa del Generalísimo

The **Copa del Generalísimo 1975 final** was the 73rd final of the King's Cup. It was played at the [Vicente Calderón Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vicente_Calder%C3%B3n_Stadium "Vicente Calderón Stadium") in [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") on 5 July 1975, [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") defeating [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") in a penalty shoot-out after a 0–0 draw.

Main article: 1974–75 Copa del Generalísimo

The **Copa del Generalísimo 1975 final** was the 73rd final of the King's Cup. It was played at the [Vicente Calderón Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vicente_Calder%C3%B3n_Stadium "Vicente Calderón Stadium") in [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") on 5 July 1975, [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") defeating [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") in a penalty shoot-out after a 0–0 draw.

The **1974–75 FA Cup** was the 94th season of the world's oldest [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football")[cup competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament "Single-elimination tournament"), the Football Association Challenge Cup, commonly known as the [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FA_Cup "FA Cup"). [West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C.") won the competition, defeating [Second Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_League_Second_Division "Football League Second Division") side [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C.") 2–0 in the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_Final "1975 FA Cup Final") at [Wembley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium_(1923) "Wembley Stadium (1923)"), London.

Matches were scheduled to be played at the stadium of the team named first on the date specified for each round, which was always a Saturday. If scores were level after 90 minutes had been played, a replay would take place at the stadium of the second-named team later the same week. If the replayed match was drawn further replays would be held until a winner was determined. If scores were level after 90 minutes had been played in a replay, a 30-minute period of [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extra_time "Extra time") would be played.

At this stage the 48 clubs from the [Football League Third](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_League_Third_Division "Football League Third Division") and [Fourth Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_League_Fourth_Division "Football League Fourth Division") joined the [non-league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-League_football "Non-League football") clubs who came through the qualifying rounds. To complete this round, non-league sides [Morecambe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morecambe_F.C. "Morecambe F.C."), [Dartford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dartford_F.C. "Dartford F.C."), [Bishop's Stortford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bishop's_Stortford_F.C. "Bishop's Stortford F.C.") and [Ilford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilford_F.C. During the 1974 close season the Football Association decided to abolish the distinction between amateur and professional clubs, resulting in the permanent cessation of the FA Amateur Cup. The annual finalists from the replacement competition for lower-level clubs, known as the [FA Vase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FA_Vase "FA Vase"), would not receive byes to the first round of the FA Cup in subsequent seasons.

The right to show FA Cup games were, as with Football League matches, shared between the BBC and ITV network. All games were shown in a highlights format, except the Final, which was shown live both on BBC1 and ITV. The BBC football highlights programme _[Match Of The Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Match\_Of\_The\_Day "Match Of The Day")_ would show up to three games and the various ITV regional network stations would cover up to one game and show highlights from other games covered elsewhere on the ITV network. No games from rounds 1 or 2 were shown. Highlights of replays would be shown on either the BBC or ITV.

The **1974–75 FA Cup** was the 94th season of the world's oldest [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football")[cup competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament "Single-elimination tournament"), the Football Association Challenge Cup, commonly known as the [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FA_Cup "FA Cup"). [West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C.") won the competition, defeating [Second Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_League_Second_Division "Football League Second Division") side [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C.") 2–0 in the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_Final "1975 FA Cup Final") at [Wembley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium_(1923) "Wembley Stadium (1923)"), London.

Matches were scheduled to be played at the stadium of the team named first on the date specified for each round, which was always a Saturday. If scores were level after 90 minutes had been played, a replay would take place at the stadium of the second-named team later the same week. If the replayed match was drawn further replays would be held until a winner was determined. If scores were level after 90 minutes had been played in a replay, a 30-minute period of [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extra_time "Extra time") would be played.

"Gateshead A.F.C."). At this stage the 48 clubs from the [Football League Third](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_League_Third_Division "Football League Third Division") and [Fourth Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_League_Fourth_Division "Football League Fourth Division") joined the [non-league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-League_football "Non-League football") clubs who came through the qualifying rounds. To complete this round, non-league sides [Morecambe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morecambe_F.C. "Morecambe F.C."), [Dartford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dartford_F.C. "Dartford F.C."), [Bishop's Stortford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bishop's_Stortford_F.C. "Bishop's Stortford F.C.") and [Ilford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilford_F.C. "Ilford F.C.") were given byes as the finalists from the previous season's [FA Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FA_Trophy "FA Trophy") and [FA Amateur Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FA_Amateur_Cup "FA Amateur Cup") respectively. During the 1974 close season the Football Association decided to abolish the distinction between amateur and professional clubs, resulting in the permanent cessation of the FA Amateur Cup. The annual finalists from the replacement competition for lower-level clubs, known as the [FA Vase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FA_Vase "FA Vase"), would not receive byes to the first round of the FA Cup in subsequent seasons.

The right to show FA Cup games were, as with Football League matches, shared between the BBC and ITV network. All games were shown in a highlights format, except the Final, which was shown live both on BBC1 and ITV. The BBC football highlights programme _[Match Of The Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Match\_Of\_The\_Day "Match Of The Day")_ would show up to three games and the various ITV regional network stations would cover up to one game and show highlights from other games covered elsewhere on the ITV network. No games from rounds 1 or 2 were shown. Highlights of replays would be shown on either the BBC or ITV.

The **1974–75 Coppa Italia** was the 28th [Coppa Italia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coppa_Italia "Coppa Italia"), the major Italian domestic cup. The competition was won by [Fiorentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACF_Fiorentina "ACF Fiorentina").

The **1974–75 Coppa Italia** was the 28th [Coppa Italia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coppa_Italia "Coppa Italia"), the major Italian domestic cup. The competition was won by [Fiorentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACF_Fiorentina "ACF Fiorentina").

The **1974–75 season** was **[Real Madrid Club de Fútbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF")'s**[72nd season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Real_Madrid_CF_seasons "List of Real Madrid CF seasons") in existence and the club's [43rd consecutive season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga_records_and_statistics#All-time_La_Liga_table "La Liga records and statistics") in the top flight of Spanish football.

## Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1974%E2%80%9375_Real_Madrid_CF_season&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Summary")]

The club clinched its 16th League title with a massive 12 points gap above runners-up [Real Zaragoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Zaragoza "Real Zaragoza") catching the first spot early since round 6 of the tournament. After collapsing to the 8th place last season, changes came to the team in the summer: replacing interim coach [Luis Molowny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Molowny "Luis Molowny")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974%E2%80%9375_Real_Madrid_CF_season#cite_note-1) arrived new head coach former [Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yugoslavia_national_football_team "Yugoslavia national football team") side manager [Miljan Miljanić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miljan_Miljani%C4%87 "Miljan Miljanić"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974%E2%80%9375_Real_Madrid_CF_season#cite_note-2)[1974 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_FIFA_World_Cup "1974 FIFA World Cup") winner [Paul Breitner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Breitner "Paul Breitner")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974%E2%80%9375_Real_Madrid_CF_season#cite_note-3) replacing [Ramón Grosso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_Grosso "Ramón Grosso") as a starter in midfield, and Argentine forward [Roberto Martínez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Mart%C3%ADnez_(footballer,_born_1946) "Roberto Martínez (footballer, born 1946)")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974%E2%80%9375_Real_Madrid_CF_season#cite_note-4) from [Español](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCD_Espanyol "RCD Espanyol") (resulting in [Oscar Más](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_M%C3%A1s "Oscar Más") being transferred out the team). Teenage defender [José Antonio Camacho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Antonio_Camacho "José Antonio Camacho") and Rubiñán reinforced the defensive line replacing Zoco (retired) and José Luis. Additionally, [Vicente del Bosque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vicente_del_Bosque "Vicente del Bosque") won the starter spot against ageing Velazquez in midfield. In the offensive line, Miljanic changed the side moving [Gunter Netzer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunter_Netzer "Gunter Netzer") from midfield to forward position along with striker Roberto Martínez, and returned from injuries was [Santillana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santillana_(footballer) "Santillana (footballer)") benching ageing Amancio. The squad scored 66 league goals, its best output in 10 seasons.

In the [1974–75 European Cup Winners' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974%E2%80%9375_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup "1974–75 European Cup Winners' Cup"), the team reached the quarter-finals being eliminated by [Crvena Zvezda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crvena_Zvezda "Crvena Zvezda") in a penalty shoot-out 5–6.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974%E2%80%9375_Real_Madrid_CF_season#cite_note-5)

Also, during June the squad clinched "[The Double](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_(association_football) "Double (association football)")" after winning the 1975 Copa del Generalísimo Final over [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") on penalties 4–3 after a 0–0 draw.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974%E2%80%9375_Real_Madrid_CF_season#cite_note-6)

The **1974–75 season** was **[Real Madrid Club de Fútbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF")'s**[72nd season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Real_Madrid_CF_seasons "List of Real Madrid CF seasons") in existence and the club's [43rd consecutive season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga_records_and_statistics#All-time_La_Liga_table "La Liga records and statistics") in the top flight of Spanish football.

## Summary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1974%E2%80%9375_Real_Madrid_CF_season&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Summary")]

The club clinched its 16th League title with a massive 12 points gap above runners-up [Real Zaragoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Zaragoza "Real Zaragoza") catching the first spot early since round 6 of the tournament. After collapsing to the 8th place last season, changes came to the team in the summer: replacing interim coach [Luis Molowny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Molowny "Luis Molowny")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974%E2%80%9375_Real_Madrid_CF_season#cite_note-1) arrived new head coach former [Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yugoslavia_national_football_team "Yugoslavia national football team") side manager [Miljan Miljanić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miljan_Miljani%C4%87 "Miljan Miljanić"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974%E2%80%9375_Real_Madrid_CF_season#cite_note-2)[1974 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974_FIFA_World_Cup "1974 FIFA World Cup") winner [Paul Breitner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Breitner "Paul Breitner")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974%E2%80%9375_Real_Madrid_CF_season#cite_note-3) replacing [Ramón Grosso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram%C3%B3n_Grosso "Ramón Grosso") as a starter in midfield, and Argentine forward [Roberto Martínez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Mart%C3%ADnez_(footballer,_born_1946) "Roberto Martínez (footballer, born 1946)")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974%E2%80%9375_Real_Madrid_CF_season#cite_note-4) from [Español](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCD_Espanyol "RCD Espanyol") (resulting in [Oscar Más](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_M%C3%A1s "Oscar Más") being transferred out the team). Teenage defender [José Antonio Camacho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Antonio_Camacho "José Antonio Camacho") and Rubiñán reinforced the defensive line replacing Zoco (retired) and José Luis. Additionally, [Vicente del Bosque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vicente_del_Bosque "Vicente del Bosque") won the starter spot against ageing Velazquez in midfield. In the offensive line, Miljanic changed the side moving [Gunter Netzer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunter_Netzer "Gunter Netzer") from midfield to forward position along with striker Roberto Martínez, and returned from injuries was [Santillana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santillana_(footballer) "Santillana (footballer)") benching ageing Amancio. The squad scored 66 league goals, its best output in 10 seasons.

In the [1974–75 European Cup Winners' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974%E2%80%9375_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup "1974–75 European Cup Winners' Cup"), the team reached the quarter-finals being eliminated by [Crvena Zvezda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crvena_Zvezda "Crvena Zvezda") in a penalty shoot-out 5–6.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974%E2%80%9375_Real_Madrid_CF_season#cite_note-5)

Also, during June the squad clinched "[The Double](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_(association_football) "Double (association football)")" after winning the 1975 Copa del Generalísimo Final over [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") on penalties 4–3 after a 0–0 draw.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1974%E2%80%9375_Real_Madrid_CF_season#cite_note-6)

The **1975 FA Cup final** was the 94th final of the [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FA_Cup "FA Cup"). It took place on 3 May 1975 at [Wembley Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium_(1923) "Wembley Stadium (1923)") and was contested by London clubs [West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C.") and [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C."). The Fulham team contained two former [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_national_football_team "England national football team") captains in former West Ham United captain [Bobby Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Moore "Bobby Moore"), making his last appearance at Wembley,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-WestHamHistory-1) and [Alan Mullery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Mullery "Alan Mullery").

West Ham United won 2–0, with both goals scored by [Alan Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Taylor_(footballer_born_1953) "Alan Taylor (footballer born 1953)"). The first came in the 60th minute when Fulham goalkeeper [Peter Mellor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Mellor "Peter Mellor") parried [Billy Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Jennings "Billy Jennings")' shot into Taylor's path and Taylor's shot went in through Mellor's legs; the second came four minutes later when Taylor capitalised after Mellor failed to hold on to [Graham Paddon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graham_Paddon "Graham Paddon")'s shot.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-2)

The 1975 West Ham United team remains the last all-English team to win the FA Cup.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-3) The match remains the only occasion that Fulham have appeared in an FA Cup final; it was the club's last major final for 35 years, until the [2010 UEFA Europa League Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_UEFA_Europa_League_Final "2010 UEFA Europa League Final").

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1975_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

[West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C.") had won the FA Cup once previously in [1964](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_FA_Cup_final "1964 FA Cup final") when they defeated [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") 3–2.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-FCHDWH-4)

Fulham had never previously played in an FA Cup final. Their previous best run was to the semi-finals in [1907–08](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1907%E2%80%9308_FA_Cup "1907–08 FA Cup") (lost 6–0 to [Newcastle United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newcastle_United_F.C. "Newcastle United F.C.")), [1935–36](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1935%E2%80%9336_FA_Cup "1935–36 FA Cup") (lost 2–1 to [Sheffield United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield_United_F.C. "Sheffield United F.C.")), [1957–58](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1957%E2%80%9358_FA_Cup "1957–58 FA Cup") (lost 5–3 to [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") in a replay) and [1961–62](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1961%E2%80%9362_FA_Cup "1961–62 FA Cup") (lost 2–1 to [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") in a replay).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-FCHDF-5)

## Route to final

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1975_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Route to final")]

### West Ham United

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1975_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: West Ham United")]

In the third round, West Ham United faced [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C.") at [The Dell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dell_(Southampton) "The Dell (Southampton)") and won 2–1. In the fourth round, they needed a replay to overcome [Swindon Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swindon_Town_F.C. "Swindon Town F.C."). After a 1–1 draw at [Upton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boleyn_Ground "Boleyn Ground"), West Ham United progressed with a 2–1 win at the [County Ground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Ground_(Swindon) "County Ground (Swindon)"). They then defeated [Queens Park Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens_Park_Rangers_F.C. "Queens Park Rangers F.C.") 2–1 at Upton Park in the fifth round. West Ham United faced [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.") at [Highbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_Stadium "Arsenal Stadium") in the quarter-finals and won 2–0. In the semi-finals, they required a replay to overcome [Ipswich Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipswich_Town_F.C. "Ipswich Town F.C."). After a goalless draw at the neutral [Villa Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villa_Park "Villa Park") in [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham "Birmingham"), West Ham United won 2–1 at [Stamford Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stamford_Bridge_(stadium) "Stamford Bridge (stadium)") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-FCHDWH-4)

### Fulham

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1975_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Fulham")]

Fulham faced [Hull City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hull_City_A.F.C. "Hull City A.F.C.") in the third round. After a 1–1 draw at [Craven Cottage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craven_Cottage "Craven Cottage") and a 2–2 draw in the replay at [Boothferry Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boothferry_Park "Boothferry Park"), Fulham advanced with a 1–0 win in the second replay at the neutral [Filbert Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filbert_Street "Filbert Street") in [Leicester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester "Leicester"). In the fourth round, they faced [Nottingham Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nottingham_Forest_F.C. "Nottingham Forest F.C."). A goalless draw at Craven Cottage was succeeded by a 1–1 draw at the [City Ground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Ground "City Ground") and a subsequent 1–1 draw, again at Craven Cottage in the second replay. Fulham eventually advanced with a 2–1 win at the City Ground in the third replay. In the fifth round, Fulham defeated [Everton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everton_F.C. "Everton F.C.") 2–1 at [Goodison Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodison_Park "Goodison Park"). They then faced [Carlisle United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlisle_United_F.C. "Carlisle United F.C.") at [Brunton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brunton_Park "Brunton Park") in the quarter-finals and won 1–0. Fulham again required a replay in their semi-final against [Birmingham City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham_City_F.C. "Birmingham City F.C."). After a 1–1 at the neutral [Hillsborough Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillsborough_Stadium "Hillsborough Stadium") in [Sheffield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield "Sheffield"), Fulham progressed to the final with a 1–0 win at [Maine Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine_Road "Maine Road") in [Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester "Manchester").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-FCHDF-5)

## Aftermath

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1975_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Aftermath")]

This was the second time that West Ham United had won the FA Cup. As defending champions the [following season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975%E2%80%9376_FA_Cup "1975–76 FA Cup"), they were eliminated at the first hurdle after losing 2–0 to [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") at Upton Park in the third round. They would win the FA Cup for a third time in [1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_FA_Cup_final "1980 FA Cup final").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-FCHDWH-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-6)

Fulham have not played in an FA Cup final since this match. Their best run in the next 50 seasons was to the semi-finals in [2001–02](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001%E2%80%9302_FA_Cup "2001–02 FA Cup") (lost 1–0 to [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.")).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-FCHDWH-4)

The **1975 FA Cup final** was the 94th final of the [FA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FA_Cup "FA Cup"). It took place on 3 May 1975 at [Wembley Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium_(1923) "Wembley Stadium (1923)") and was contested by London clubs [West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C.") and [Fulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulham_F.C. "Fulham F.C."). The Fulham team contained two former [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_national_football_team "England national football team") captains in former West Ham United captain [Bobby Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Moore "Bobby Moore"), making his last appearance at Wembley,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-WestHamHistory-1) and [Alan Mullery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Mullery "Alan Mullery").

West Ham United won 2–0, with both goals scored by [Alan Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Taylor_(footballer_born_1953) "Alan Taylor (footballer born 1953)"). The first came in the 60th minute when Fulham goalkeeper [Peter Mellor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Mellor "Peter Mellor") parried [Billy Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Jennings "Billy Jennings")' shot into Taylor's path and Taylor's shot went in through Mellor's legs; the second came four minutes later when Taylor capitalised after Mellor failed to hold on to [Graham Paddon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graham_Paddon "Graham Paddon")'s shot.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-2)

The 1975 West Ham United team remains the last all-English team to win the FA Cup.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-3) The match remains the only occasion that Fulham have appeared in an FA Cup final; it was the club's last major final for 35 years, until the [2010 UEFA Europa League Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_UEFA_Europa_League_Final "2010 UEFA Europa League Final").

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1975_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

[West Ham United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Ham_United_F.C. "West Ham United F.C.") had won the FA Cup once previously in [1964](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_FA_Cup_final "1964 FA Cup final") when they defeated [Preston North End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_North_End_F.C. "Preston North End F.C.") 3–2.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-FCHDWH-4)

Fulham had never previously played in an FA Cup final. Their previous best run was to the semi-finals in [1907–08](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1907%E2%80%9308_FA_Cup "1907–08 FA Cup") (lost 6–0 to [Newcastle United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newcastle_United_F.C. "Newcastle United F.C.")), [1935–36](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1935%E2%80%9336_FA_Cup "1935–36 FA Cup") (lost 2–1 to [Sheffield United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield_United_F.C. "Sheffield United F.C.")), [1957–58](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1957%E2%80%9358_FA_Cup "1957–58 FA Cup") (lost 5–3 to [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") in a replay) and [1961–62](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1961%E2%80%9362_FA_Cup "1961–62 FA Cup") (lost 2–1 to [Burnley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnley_F.C. "Burnley F.C.") in a replay).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-FCHDF-5)

## Route to final

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1975_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Route to final")]

### West Ham United

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1975_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: West Ham United")]

In the third round, West Ham United faced [Southampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southampton_F.C. "Southampton F.C.") at [The Dell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dell_(Southampton) "The Dell (Southampton)") and won 2–1. In the fourth round, they needed a replay to overcome [Swindon Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swindon_Town_F.C. "Swindon Town F.C."). After a 1–1 draw at [Upton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boleyn_Ground "Boleyn Ground"), West Ham United progressed with a 2–1 win at the [County Ground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Ground_(Swindon) "County Ground (Swindon)"). They then defeated [Queens Park Rangers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens_Park_Rangers_F.C. "Queens Park Rangers F.C.") 2–1 at Upton Park in the fifth round. West Ham United faced [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.") at [Highbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_Stadium "Arsenal Stadium") in the quarter-finals and won 2–0. In the semi-finals, they required a replay to overcome [Ipswich Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipswich_Town_F.C. "Ipswich Town F.C."). After a goalless draw at the neutral [Villa Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villa_Park "Villa Park") in [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham "Birmingham"), West Ham United won 2–1 at [Stamford Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stamford_Bridge_(stadium) "Stamford Bridge (stadium)") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-FCHDWH-4)

### Fulham

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=1975_FA_Cup_final&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Fulham")]

Fulham faced [Hull City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hull_City_A.F.C. "Hull City A.F.C.") in the third round. After a 1–1 draw at [Craven Cottage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craven_Cottage "Craven Cottage") and a 2–2 draw in the replay at [Boothferry Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boothferry_Park "Boothferry Park"), Fulham advanced with a 1–0 win in the second replay at the neutral [Filbert Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filbert_Street "Filbert Street") in [Leicester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leicester "Leicester"). In the fourth round, they faced [Nottingham Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nottingham_Forest_F.C. "Nottingham Forest F.C."). A goalless draw at Craven Cottage was succeeded by a 1–1 draw at the [City Ground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Ground "City Ground") and a subsequent 1–1 draw, again at Craven Cottage in the second replay. Fulham eventually advanced with a 2–1 win at the City Ground in the third replay. In the fifth round, Fulham defeated [Everton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everton_F.C. "Everton F.C.") 2–1 at [Goodison Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodison_Park "Goodison Park"). They then faced [Carlisle United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlisle_United_F.C. "Carlisle United F.C.") at [Brunton Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brunton_Park "Brunton Park") in the quarter-finals and won 1–0. Fulham again required a replay in their semi-final against [Birmingham City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham_City_F.C. "Birmingham City F.C."). After a 1–1 at the neutral [Hillsborough Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillsborough_Stadium "Hillsborough Stadium") in [Sheffield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield "Sheffield"), Fulham progressed to the final with a 1–0 win at [Maine Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine_Road "Maine Road") in [Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester "Manchester").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_FA_Cup_final#cite_note-FCHDF-5)
